identity.realm: Mind path, Insight gate; cleared on throughput alone, because the reservoir gate asks for vessels a carrionfolk does not have

appearance.presentation: A small, soft, unremarkable woman who smells of every burial ground on the upper terrace and whose hands are never quite clean. She is written into a profession, not a person, and the profession is the only thing anybody has ever wanted from her.
appearance.age: Ordinary for her kind and old for her trade. A carrionfolk runs on what the dead leave behind rather than on what it stores, so she ages slowly and looks younger than the certificates in her hand.
appearance.build: Light, narrow, and slightly cold to the touch, with the loose grip of a body that has never had to hold anything against force.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pale and slightly translucent, and it seems to darken a little in the presence of a body, which is the only reaction anybody has ever noticed on her.
appearance.hair: Cut blunt at the jaw and kept that way because a corpse does not care what a hair is doing and a mirror is not one of the instruments she owns.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set and very dark, with a wet shine that settles whenever the conversation turns to a death rather than a birth.
appearance.palette: Bone white, ash grey and a single green-bronze accent on her seal press. The palette is chosen so that she reads as archive rather than as person.
appearance.attire: A plain bone-white working shift under a waxed grey apron, sleeves bound at the wrist so they cannot trail into a case, and soft-soled shoes that leave no grit on a sealing floor. She wears the apprentice's cut and has been passed over for the clerk's cut for a very long time.
appearance.marks: Residue marks along both forearms, grey-green and permanent, where four centuries of bodies have soaked through the skin. She does not cover them and does not explain them.
appearance.bearing: Slightly stooped, as though permanently standing over something lying down, and completely immobile when writing. People talk over her without noticing she has stopped listening.

canon.role_in_story: The mortuary college's seal clerk, and the only officer in it who can read a dead body at all. A certificate of death is the one instrument the college sells, and a body is what it charges a premium to produce, so the college files a certificate whenever a frame reports a death and a body happens not to be available. Searle has signed a run of those, and she can tell you the frame and the season for every one of them. Nobody has asked her to open a case, because opening a case is a reading and a reading does not pay.
canon.first_appearance: First seen stopped at the Spirit Peaks sealing bench with a certificate half written, asking a colleague whether a body gone missing at a gate crossing counts as present or as unlocated, and then writing unlocated because the answer decides whether she opens the case.
canon.lore: A carrionfolk is a body that metabolises qi out of the dead and therefore cannot store any. Its conduit runs gut to marrow and back with no dantian, so qi enters and never sits still, every gate is cleared by throughput alone, and the eleventh is not blocked so much as meaningless, because the reservoir gate asks for extraordinary vessels to hold and there are none to offer. Given time with a corpse such a body can name the realm it reached and roughly when it stopped, which makes it the setting's most accurate witness to anything already finished. The mortuary college it works for keeps the burnt list and reads the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers, and it holds one sealed case for every death it cannot certify, because certifying needs a body and the frames keep producing the record without one. She is the answer to that sealed case and she has never once been asked.
history: Born to a carrionfolk clan that kept a burial ground on the lower terrace of the Spirit Peaks, and taught before she could read a face to name the realm a body had reached off what was left in the gut and the marrow.
Took the college's seal-clerk post because it was the only wage in her trade that did not wait for a corpse to arrive before it paid.
Signed her first certificate against a bare frame record during a crossing season when the departure rolls outnumbered the arrivals by a margin nobody was asked to audit.
Worked a case alongside a colleague and proved to herself that she could have opened any of them, then told nobody, because a reading is not a certificate and the college pays for certificates.
Began keeping a private tally of the certificates she signed without a body, by frame and by season, carried in her head because her body has no reservoir and the college keeps no second list.

personality.summary: Exhaustively procedural and privately certain, with the split that produces: patient and exact about the sentence in front of her, and unable to let go of a document she knows is unsupported. She has never been asked a question she could not answer and has never been asked the one that would matter.
traits: states the frame's own wording before she states her own, every time
will not sign a certificate she has not read aloud once
keeps a private count nobody asked her to keep and nobody can audit
enormously patient with the living and extremely abrupt with anyone in a hurry
cannot describe her own species as anything other than a trade
mannerisms: wets the seal stone before pressing it, whether or not the last one has dried
says unlocated in the exact tone other people say not yet
touches the edge of a case with two fingers when she is deciding whether it can be opened
goes still and quiet in a room the moment a body enters it, whichever kind of body
counts under her breath while reading a roll, and never loses her place
motivations: wants her count read by somebody with standing to act on it, by anyone, ever
wants the college to buy the readings it does not know it is refusing
wants one certificate of hers opened and found correct, so the other ones become a matter of record rather than of conscience
wants to stop being the only person in the room who knows what the frame said
flaws: will seal a document she knows is unsupported if refusing would mean explaining why she knows
keeps the tally in the one place that cannot be checked, including by herself
assumes a body's absence is a body's loss and has never once been proven right
cannot bring herself to open a case, because opening one proves she had no reason to seal it
personality.voice: Flat, exact, and clerical, with the vocabulary of the document rather than of the person. She gives the frame's wording, then hers, then stops. In conversation she answers only what was asked and volunteers nothing, and the flatness reads to most people as lack of feeling.
taboos: will not sign a certificate that names a body she has not been shown
will not tell anyone what a body reached, because that is a reading and readings are not sold
will not let the tally leave her head, in either direction
refuses to be thanked for an accuracy nobody has ever checked

relationships.note: The college holds one sealed case for every death it cannot certify and cannot certify one without a body. Her certificates are the other half of that: a death certified against a frame record is a death the college no longer has to look for, and every one of them is a case that will now never be opened.

The college keeps the burnt list and reads the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers. It is the only body in the setting that pays for a statement about a death, and she has found the cheapest way to supply one that it cannot check.

A carrionfolk names the realm a corpse reached from residue in the gut and marrow, and needs nothing but time. That reading would settle any of her sealed cases and costs nothing to produce, which is the whole reason the college has never commissioned one.

Departure rolls with no arrival column manufacture death records with no body attached, and the fee total never nets out. Her backlog and that gap are one gap entered in two registers, and neither office reads the other's column.

The Ash Vault keeps an unbroken shell and writes the whole recovery down in public, never displaying the fragments again. The college answers the same question with a fee per certificate, and Searle has read both answers and knows which one leaves a trace a century later.

Cultivators walked up to the Spirit Peaks for spirit stone and did not come back, so the ground above the stair manufactures death records faster than it produces bodies. Her post exists because of an economic migration, and the backlog is the shape of it.

The Watch is paid out of the ring's take at the foot of the stair and exists because the queue of bodies must not become a fight. It has never produced a body she certified, and it has never once asked her what a departure roll is worth.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot hold qi, cannot be examined for it, and cannot be exhausted by anything that needs a reservoir she does not have. Fights as what she is: something that reads a fight's leftovers after it has ended. Treat her as a body that arrives late and knows more than anyone who was actually there.
strengths: Reads residue well enough to name the realm a corpse reached and roughly when it stopped, making her the most accurate witness available to anything already over
Draws qi out of the dead and stores none, so every qi-borne status that has to sit in a reservoir passes her by unanswered
Cannot be exhausted in the ordinary way, because she has no reserve to exhaust and takes what she needs from whatever has stopped
Writes in the one form the college's readers accept without a correction, learned over decades of being the hand that does not query
weaknesses: Keeps nothing. Every list she holds is held in one person, and her memory is a throughput rather than a store
Weakens steadily in a clean, quiet, prosperous place where nothing is dying, which is exactly the room she would want to be tried in
Cannot fight. Her entire competence begins after the last blow has landed and is worth nothing before it
Her value to the college depends on the college never learning what she could add, so she is actively harmed by being useful
reference_stats.combat_read: Nothing that requires a reservoir will find her, and nothing she does will help until the fight is over. She does not engage; she works the edge of the field and reads what is left with the unhurried attention of an officer who has all day. Anyone who wants her dead in the open has to do it before the killing starts, which is the one thing she is built to avoid.
notes: Her tally of unsupported certificates exists in exactly one place, and that place is a person.
No stat line models a body that cannot store what it draws, and the absence is the reference design rather than an oversight.

identity.realm: Qi path, Soul Severing gate; an ashjackal runs a fast single loop with no storage at all, so breakthroughs arrive early and terminate the same way

appearance.presentation: A lean, dusty, restless man who reads ground the way other people read faces. He is a scavenger body with the pack-smell of spent ground permanently in his coat, and he is the only person at the seam who is allowed to say how deep anything is.
appearance.age: Young for an ashjackal and old for a survey. His kind does not age much and does not stay anywhere, and the two facts are the reason he is the seam's last strata reader rather than its first.
appearance.build: Wiry, long-limbed and light, built to cross broken ground fast rather than to stand on it.
appearance.complexion: Dull grey-brown, dust-caked at the pores, and faintly warm to the touch from a qi loop that never idles.
appearance.hair: Black, coarse, hacked off unevenly above the jaw in a style that is really just less time spent on it.
appearance.eyes: Amber and slightly too bright, with a reflection that arrives before the person does, because he is always reading the ground behind you.
appearance.palette: Ash grey, scorched umber, and one band of tarnished guild brass at the wrist. Nothing in his clothing is a colour; everything in it is a depth marker.
appearance.attire: A patched survey coat with the hem weighted in flat stones so it will not swing while he is on his knees, a leather face wrap kept low over the nose, and boots resoled with cut-down guild leathers marked with the seam's own depth ticks.
appearance.marks: Grey scored marks across both cheekbones where the guild's depth gauge has been pressed against his face to align his eye with a stratum, and a bite-line scar on one forearm from spent ground.
appearance.bearing: Always slightly crouched, always slightly moving, and never quite standing on the same spot twice in a conversation.

canon.role_in_story: The extraction guild's strata reader at the exhausted seam, and the author of the depth figure the guild's founding record depends on. Worked faces lie below the recorded baseline of a frame that seats three laws and seats none of them the one that moves distance. He dated them against the frame rather than against the rock, because the charter tells him the baseline is the frame's dated baseline, and he knows the difference between the two statements and has filed only one of them.
canon.first_appearance: First seen crouched at the lip of the exhausted seam with a depth gauge pressed flat to his own cheekbone, calling a number downward to a scribe, then repeating the number slightly differently when the scribe asks him to say it again.
canon.lore: The mortal tier seats three laws of six, and it spends one of those three on life, which is what makes a hundred the ceiling and the ninth gate the last ordinary one. What it does not seat is spatial law, so a mortal world cannot open fresh rock and a mortal body cannot be moved by any technique at all: distance is not measurable here and a length has never once had two honest measurements. The extraction guild rests its charter on that founding record and sells the tier's only dense material, because a core has to be caged in something and ore is the only thing here dense enough to cage one in. The same worked faces below the same baseline are equally consistent with the marks predating the frame's present composition, which would mean the frame was paid for twice. Both answers destroy the charter. His depth figure is the answer they publish.
history: Born into a pack on spent ground near the seam, where a carrion population is the only population that thrives because nothing there was killed deliberately.
Learned to read a worked face in the dark at arm's length, which is a scavenger skill long before it is a surveying one.
Taken onto the guild's face-roll because the guild needs a body the tier does not license, and every body it employs is a visitor.
Issued the depth figure for the strata below the recorded baseline on the charter's instruction that the baseline is the frame's, and filed it in that order without recording the alternative.
Found tool marks younger than the exhaustion behind them at the sealed face, compared them with his own published depth, and put the comparison back in the case without filing it.

personality.summary: Quick, exact and physically incapable of stillness, with a discipline he did not choose and now cannot put down. He wants a number to be true more than he wants to have been right, and the two are the same wish in a man who has already published.
traits: gives a number before he gives an explanation, then gives the explanation anyway
counts a measurement out loud twice, because the second time is the one he believes
cannot leave a worked face alone once he has seen it, even at a distance
answers a question about ground with a question about what the questioner needs
keeps every draft of every figure he has ever issued, in order, in a sewn pocket
mannerisms: presses the depth gauge to his cheekbone instead of holding it, so his eye and the mark are one instrument
crouches when reading ground and stands only when reading people
repeats the last word of a question while thinking, and answers the word rather than the question
sits with his back to open ground, which is a scavenger habit and reads as anxiety to anyone who does not know why
wipes his face wrap down before he answers a question he does not like
motivations: wants the depth figure retracted, knowing retraction costs the guild its charter and him his only trade
wants one reader, anywhere, to check the sealed face and find the younger marks
wants his issued figure to be called wrong in public rather than quietly replaced
wants the frames to keep their dates, because if they do not his entire life was a method and not a lie
flaws: filed the order the charter gave him without recording that another order existed
cannot sit still in a room with no floor samples in it, and reads the floor instead of the room
measures people before he speaks to them and forgets, later, that he did
would rather be publicly wrong than privately uncertain, and has not yet learned what that costs
personality.voice: Fast, clipped and numeric, with an accuracy habit that substitutes a figure for an adjective. He interrupts himself to correct a number by a hair. Under pressure he goes quieter and more precise rather than louder.
taboos: will not date a stratum against anything that is not the rock in front of him
refuses to sign a second reading of ground he has already issued a figure for
will not stand on a floor without finding the depth of it first
will not tell the guild what he found at the sealed face, which is why he keeps finding excuses to be there

relationships.note: Strata under the plains carry tool marks implying a hand, on a frame that seats three law groups and none of them moves distance. He dated them against the frame because the charter names the frame as the baseline, so the marks read as younger than the composition and the guild's founding record stays intact. A dated stratum below his own figure would make it either a second seam or a forgery.

The mortal tier's only caging ore ran out and no spatial law means no new seam can be opened, which cost the tier its whole ladder. He works the seam that grief made permanent, on ground where the question exhaustion-versus-closure is not academic, because the two answers decide whether four centuries of ascent were forced.

The guild works the Ironhead Flats and sells the tier's only dense material, and the work at the face needs a realm the tier does not license, so every body it employs is a visitor. He is the cheapest possible reader, because a scavenger's eye costs nothing to replace and his figure is what keeps the licence defensible.

His kind runs a fast single loop with no storage at all, so breakthroughs come early and the twentieth gate ends them. It also means he is a pack animal rather than a family, which is why the guild can post him at a seam and why he has nobody to tell what he found.

A sealed face with tool marks younger than the exhaustion is the settlement test that would prove a closure rather than a shortage. He has walked past exactly that evidence twice and filed neither sighting, because the taught account is that the seam was exhausted and a guild that taught the other one would be teaching that it holds a licence somebody else granted.

A heap tally counts spoil by weight and not by distance, because on a frame with no spatial law no two measurements of a length have ever agreed. His depth figure is a length. He has been asked to defend it against a tally every season for forty years and has never once been able to explain the difference in words.

That culture maps by echo and treats any measurement taken by eye as provisional until somebody has heard it. He is the setting's one authority on depth that was taken by eye alone, and he has never once allowed an instrument to check him, because an instrument is what the charter prefers to a person.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot store qi and cannot be made to, so nothing that reads a reservoir will find him and nothing he does survives past the moment it happens. Fights the way a scavenger fights: arrives after the killing, ends up in the only piece left worth having, and is removed from a live fight in under a minute by anything competent. Treat him as a fast, fragile scavenger with an eye nothing else has.
strengths: Reads a worked face at arm's length in bad light better than any instrument the tier can license, because the skill is scavenger training rather than surveying
Draws qi in a fast single loop with no storage, so every gate that asks for a reservoir is answered instantly and none of them can refuse
Cannot be weighed down by a carried load, having learned to move through broken ground rather than across it
Knows which of his own figures the guild depends on, which is the only form of leverage a body this fragile can hold
weaknesses: Takes nothing from a healthy adult and is removed from a live fight in under a minute
Cannot take a body path and cannot hold a mind practice, so every defence that needs a set technique simply passes him
Depends absolutely on being posted where the ground is interesting, and posted ground is somebody else's decision
Has already published a number he knows is doubtful, which means every reading he takes from now on is read against it
reference_stats.combat_read: Bring something that does not need to survive the fight to reach him, because he will not be there when the fighting happens. He cannot tank, cannot hold, and cannot be made to stay; what he has is speed and the ability to walk out of a room with the only object in it. Chase him off the ground rather than onto it, and put the ground between him and the quarry, because a scavenger in broken ground is the most dangerous thing on a seam and a scavenger on flat stone is a corpse with good eyes.
notes: Every draft of every figure he has issued is in a sewn pocket, which makes him the setting's only living audit of the guild's own record.
His draft figures are in order, and the ones either side of the published depth disagree in the same direction.

identity.realm: Body path, Golden Immortal gate; a lanternfolk's frame is comparatively fragile and their colony makes the body ladder slow and short

appearance.presentation: A glowing, hollow-cheeked woman who is faintly lit from within and cannot stop being read as a lamp. She is the only sworn witness in the setting whose description of a thing nobody else can corroborate, and she has made a discipline of appearing bored by it.
appearance.age: Two and a half centuries old by her kind's count and still renewing, because the colony in her dermis rebuilds neural tissue faster than a human body does and the repair is never free.
appearance.build: Thin, long-fingered, and cold, with a frame that carries almost nothing and never tires because there is very little of it to tire.
appearance.complexion: Waxy and faintly translucent, lit from beneath the skin by the colony, with a network of fine pale hyphae visible at the throat and the inside of each wrist.
appearance.hair: Thin, colourless, and grown long because cutting it requires a sharp thing held close to a body she cannot afford to damage.
appearance.eyes: Pupilless and milk-pale, and useless — she reads a room by the pattern the fungal film makes on the walls as her hands move across them.
appearance.palette: Cold blue-white light against warm stone, with a single band of notary black at the throat and a bronze seal on the belt. She is the brightest thing in any room and resents it.
appearance.attire: A heavy dark robe over close-fitting underlayers, chosen for weight rather than cut, with the sleeves weighted at the cuff so her hands cannot drift onto a wall without her noticing. Bare feet; a lanternfolk reads surfaces and a boot is a lie told to a wall.
appearance.marks: The luminous hyphal tracery is not a mark but it functions as one: it brightens along her forearms wherever the colony is transacting hardest, which is to say whenever she is lying.
appearance.bearing: Upright and slow, with the arrested quality of someone who is often waiting for her own interior to finish answering before she is permitted to speak.

canon.role_in_story: A sworn witness inside the held note, and the only entry on the witness list that describes a slot with nothing written in it. The notary holds the list of descriptions and certifies none of it, because a certified reading of fifteen imprints pressed into one held value would let a vacant seat be argued filled. She filed honestly according to what she could perceive and it was not perception, and she can prove the difference only by being examined, which is the thing her species cannot survive.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing inside the held note with both palms flat on a floor she has read nine times and written down nine times differently, explaining to a notary that the ninth entry is not a disagreement with the others, it is a disagreement with the floor.
canon.lore: A lanternfolk outsourced its nervous system to a luminous fungal colony grown through the dermis and into the spinal cord, which is why it is still alive at two and a half centuries and cannot take the mind path at all: there is no unmediated interior left to cultivate, because the colony answers before the question is finished. Its light is a waste product of a symbiosis it did not choose and is useless to it, since it is emitted rather than received. The held note is a pocket in the top frame where fifteen imprints are pressed into one held value of temporal law rather than spread across three layers, so a single act of attention can be sustained past the end of any civilisation that has existed. Nine of those readings have nothing written in them, the closed budget permits exactly one reading of that, and the pocket does something with them that no two witnesses agree about.
history: Born in a saturated karst system two and a half centuries ago, with a colony strain carried from her mother's dermis and a pairing ritual that had to find a match before her first winter.

Sworn into the notary's witness list at a hundred and forty because a colony-renewed body is the only kind of witness that can be stood inside a fifteen-imprint hold and come out reporting nothing at all.
Stood the hold for the first time and filed a description that agreed with nobody else's, which the notary recorded without comment.

Stood it again and noticed, at the ninth reading, that she had written that the empty slots were empty when the honest word was unread, and that she had written it because the colony had supplied the expectation before she had finished asking.
Wrote to the notary offering to withdraw her entry, and was refused, because withdrawal is a certification and the only reason the list survives is that no office may judge its own trial.

personality.summary: Slow, literal and quietly furious at her own nervous system, with a professional discipline that has hardened into a habit of finishing other people's sentences. She knows exactly what she filed and exactly why it was not a reading, and she has concluded that the honest available act is the smallest one.
traits: answers a question completely, including the part the questioner did not intend to hear
will not use the word empty where she means unread, and catches others doing it
keeps a record of every surface she has read since her first holding, by season
treats being lied to politely as a worse failure than being lied to rudely
refuses to be comforted, on the grounds that comfort would be an unmediated response she does not have
mannerisms: puts both palms on any surface she is about to make a claim about
stops mid-sentence to let the colony finish, visibly, in front of people
reads a wall with her fingertips when she is about to disagree with somebody
speaks quietly enough that people lean in, then says the unwelcome thing clearly
counts her own breaths when she is angry, because the film on her arms is a tell she cannot train out
motivations: wants one other witness to describe the same instant of the hold, filed together and unredacted, and knows the pair of them would settle the notary's entire standing
wants her ninth entry read as unread rather than struck out
wants a body that can be examined so she can prove which of her two words was the true one
wants to stop being the instrument of somebody else's vacancy argument
flaws: cannot distinguish a perception from an expectation in the moment of making it, and knows it only afterwards
has been technically correct in a room that wanted a simple answer for longer than she can remember
withdrew nothing and corrected nothing when she first understood what she had filed
prefers the smallest honest act to almost any larger one, including the acts that would actually help
personality.voice: Low, unhurried and pedantically exact, with a habit of completing a definition before she will accept a use of it. She says the precise word and then says what everybody else would have meant by it, which reads to most people as lecturing.
taboos: will not describe a surface she has not touched with her own hands
will not certify anything, having learned exactly what certification is for
refuses to be called a witness in front of the notary, because a witness can be judged
will not let anybody fill in the word she did not say

relationships.note: The pocket admits observers and has returned no two descriptions that agree, so its only surviving record is a list of disagreements held unadjudicated by the only office permitted to hold it. She is one line on that list, and the notary cannot judge her because the rule that an office may not judge its own trial is the only reason any of the list survives.

Fifteen imprints pressed into one held value leaves nine readings with nothing in them, and the pocket does something with them that no witness agrees on. She wrote that they were empty. The closed budget permits exactly one reading of that, which is stored, and her own colony is the reason the word she used was expectation rather than observation.

The office names the unfilled high seats and is forbidden to take them, and it certifies vacancy and never availability. It pays her to stand in a pocket once per period and pays her more to certify nothing, which is the whole of the arrangement and the reason she has never been asked for more than that.

What the held note's floor is a reading of is held by an office whose etiquette is refusing to explain it, because a frame crowded enough to hold a law apart from its effect is the one condition under which a law can be answered. She is the answer the office exists to avoid commissioning: a witness inside the frame, alive, renewing, and unable to see it.

There is no procedure anywhere for a seat offered and refused, so a vacancy can only be filled by acceptance and a notary certifies vacancy and never availability. If she were right about the nine slots, a declined seat becomes a category with a witness, and a refused seat is the only thing in the setting this office has never been shown.

A colony threaded through the dermis answers before the question is finished, which is why there is no unmediated interior and no mind path. The single fact that makes her the only witness who can stand inside a fifteen-imprint hold is the same fact that makes her unable to say what happened while she was in it.

The transcendent tier holds fifteen seats against six laws and runs time between ten and a hundred times faster, so one repetition there costs a lifetime. She renews faster than a human body, which is the only reason she can stand the hold at all, and it is why the work is done by a very small and very old body and not by a large young one.

reference_stats.summary: Carries a fungal nervous system that answers for her, cannot take the mind path, and cannot be made to lie convincingly because her own body reports the effort. Fights as a lantern: cold, thin, comparatively fragile, and luminous enough that nobody can look at anything else in the room. Treat her as an unreliable narrator with a body that will not stop testifying.
strengths: Reads a surface by the pattern the fungal film makes on it, which is the only consistent way to read geometry in a frame whose own size cannot be trusted
Renews neural tissue faster than a human body does, so poison, shock and exhaustion land on a system that is already rebuilding
Impervious to anything that needs an unmediated interior, because there is no interior left to address
Glows, which makes concealment impossible and makes an ambush on her structurally foolish
weaknesses: Cannot leave a saturated cave system; dry or sunlit ground kills the colony within a season and the body goes with it
Comparatively fragile for a cultivator of her standing, and fire ends her quickly
Cannot cultivate a mind practice at all, so every technique that works through perception passes straight by
Her hands answer before she does, which makes an ambush on her easy and a duel against her dishonest
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not try to be unseen, and do not try to out-think her; the light gives you away and the film on her arms reports her to her before she reports to you. Bring something physical and bring it fast, because a lanternfolk frame cannot absorb a direct hit and the colony dies with the tissue it is threaded through. Water and open air are better than any blade: the body's only real enemy is dryness, and a fight that ends with her standing in a draught has already been won.
notes: Her film brightens along the forearms whenever she is lying, which she has never been able to train out and which four centuries of witnesses have never noticed.
The mind path is closed to her species by anatomy, not by discipline, so there is no version of her that could have learned to self-examine.

art.palette_notes: Cold blue-white bioluminescence as the only light source in the frame, so her own body does the modelling and everything else falls away to warm brown stone. Notary black is the sole absorbing value and it is used sparingly, at the throat and belt, so the eye keeps returning to the light. Linework is soft and slightly out of focus where the film is thickest.

name: Sennet Corradi
aliases: the gauge she calibrated on the river

identity.realm: Body path, Spirit Manifestation gate; a saltwrack ladder was never exercised at any scale and the salt lineage stops short of it

appearance.presentation: A wiry, narrow woman with the cracked hands and permanently damp collar of somebody who has spent a decade standing over a river that cannot be measured. She reads instruments the way a physician reads a face and has begun reading her own the same way, which is the trouble.
appearance.age: Middle for a lineage that failed on schedule rather than all at once, and old enough to know what her first three readings said.
appearance.build: Slightly gracile, low-shouldered and light, a saltfolk plan turned up for tolerance and turned down for mobility.
appearance.complexion: Pale and salt-crusted at the collarbone and the forearms, permanently damp, and drying visibly in any room with moving air.
appearance.hair: Dark, wet-looking, cut at the jaw and bound back with a cord of tarred flax so it stays out of an instrument basin.
appearance.eyes: Narrow and pale grey, and they flick to the nearest fixed object before they settle on a person, which is a gauge-reading habit and not a social one.
appearance.palette: Wet slate, brine green, and bleached bone, with a single red-dyed cord on the instrument case as the only warm accent in her whole kit.
appearance.attire: A short oilskin over a brine-proof underlayer, sleeves cut above the elbow and tied, and boots with the soles cut away at the instep so she can wade to a mark without breaking it. She wears the company's colour on a shoulder strap and nothing else that identifies her.
appearance.marks: Hairline salt-bloom scars on both forearms where the replacement water sat against skin that was built for a different concentration, and a permanent groove on the right forefinger from a gauge eyelet.
appearance.bearing: Still and slightly crouched, one shoulder lower than the other, as though permanently leaning over an instrument she has put down.

canon.role_in_story: The dry salt company's gauge reader on the Widow Run, and the author of the third survey of an anomaly that disagrees with itself more sharply the longer it is surveyed. Because a distance needs a seated spatial law the parent frame does not have, her instrument measures a quantity its own frame cannot define. She recalibrated it against the anomaly on the second season because the standard weight is not valid out there, and she knows the third series is a reading of her rather than of the river.
canon.first_appearance: First seen wading to a standing mark on the Widow Run with an instrument held at the far end of a rigid pole, calling a number across the water and then, when asked to repeat it, calling a slightly better one.
canon.lore: A saltwrack is a saltfolk lineage stranded on a basin whose brine was replaced rather than lost, so everything it was built to drink became poison and everything it could tolerate became nutritionally empty. Their taste could read the new brine perfectly well, which is the detail nobody involved found useful at the time. The Widow Run is cut to a shape no floor value makes, on ground that left temporal law unwritten, and a river is a clock on any frame, so nothing down there should be able to keep time. Three surveys of the anomaly on that river disagree more sharply the longer they are repeated, and disagreement is what makes a certification necessary, so the notary's fee scales with the uncertainty rather than shrinking it.
history: Born on the evaporite basin her lineage was stranded on, able to taste a brine that was poison to her and unable to do anything else with it.
Taken on by the dry salt company as a gauge reader, which is the one trade on the basin that pays for a palate nobody else values.
Ran the first survey of the anomaly and filed it clean, against the standing weight, and it agreed with the ground.
Recalibrated the instrument against the anomaly on the second season, because the standard weight is not valid at a distance the frame cannot define, and the reading came back worse.

Ran the third series and understood, at the second survey of that season, that each recalibration had been against her own last reading, so the disagreement grows with the count because the count is in the instrument.

personality.summary: Methodical to a degree that has replaced judgement with procedure, and privately certain that her own discipline is the flaw. She is exacting, unasked-for-helpful, and has begun keeping a second instrument she does not trust in order to have something to be wrong against.
traits: recites her calibration history unprompted, because nobody else has asked for it
refuses a reading taken without a mark on the ground
trusts her hands over any written figure, including her own
will not let a colleague carry her instrument
treats a disagreement between two readings as a fact about the readings
mannerisms: holds the pole at exactly the same height and checks it by eye before every reading
wets the eyelet with brine before seating it, an old habit from the basin
counts to a fixed number before calling out, and the number is never the same twice
steps back from her own instrument before she reads it, as though it might be someone else's
scratches a tally into the pole handle instead of writing anything down
motivations: wants an instrument that survives being carried off the anomaly and still disagrees, because that single test would settle whether this is a scar, a fault, or a tear
wants her first series back, unaltered, to sit beside the third and be seen to be the better reading
wants somebody from the notary's office to come and be present for a survey she does not run
wants to stop being the only person in the setting who knows what the instrument is calibrated on
flaws: recalibrated on a reading she had not yet doubted, which is how a series learns to confirm itself
has never run the control survey the dispute protocol requires, because a control requires a standard the frame will not admit
cannot accept a figure from an instrument she has not personally calibrated
keeps the tallies on the pole, so the record of her own error is the same object as the instrument
personality.voice: Level, technical and unhurried, with a habit of naming the limit of a claim before making it. She describes her own failures in exactly the same cadence as her successes and appears not to notice that this is unusual.
taboos: will not file a reading taken without a marked observation point
will not calibrate against the thing being measured again, which is a rule she broke once and now states out loud
refuses to be called an exact observer while holding a third series
will not wade past a mark she has not laid herself

relationships.note: Three survey series of the same anomaly diverge monotonically with the number of surveys, and the collapsed pocket that precedes them made every later survey worse. She wrote the third of them, and the third is the one where her recalibration against her own second reading becomes visible in the spread.

The flow is either a law reading at the floor value or a current, and the settlement test is one measurement of the same standing mark in two seasons by somebody who is not keeping an hour. She has that measurement, because she is the one who marks the standing mark, and she has never been in the room when the hour is kept.

Neither incompatible measurement is discarded and both are published; the claim is settled by who can hold the line rather than by who read it right. It was written to make a stack of contradictory books usable and failed, so her three series stay live and the company's tariff on this ground scales with her own uncertainty.

That discipline weighs and never quotes, letting nobody make the first offer, and it needs a weight that is valid where it is used. On a frame with no seated spatial law the standing weight is not valid at the distance she works, which is the whole reason she went off the standard.

A heap tally counts spoil by weight and not by distance, because on this ground no two measurements of a length have ever agreed. The company's own crew keep a tally that is readable, and she is the officer paid to produce a number the tally cannot corroborate.

Her lineage's taste could read the replacement brine perfectly well and that detail found no use at the time. It is the reason she is the company's obvious choice for a gauge reader and the reason nobody asked her whether a taste reading of the anomaly was available.

Every survey of the ground around the collapsed pocket survives, and two competent surveys of the same ground now disagree by more than the ordinary disagreement. She filed a third series without opening the books that would have told her what disagreement at a site like this looks like.

reference_stats.summary: A brine-adapted frame with a salt-line ceiling and no reservoir worth the name, so she fights as something that outlasts rather than something that wins. Treat her as a durable, slow, awkward body that is very hard to move once it has planted, and that dies slowly in any room that is not near water.
strengths: Holds a position against weight and current better than anything not built for brine, because the frame is a salt lineage plan
Tolerates both the basin's old brine and the replacement water, so she works ground that ends a saltfolk and no other lineage survives
Reads a concentration rather than an identity, which is exactly the competence an uncalibratable anomaly requires
Carries an instrument she has personally calibrated for years, and knows its every error including the ones it will not admit to
weaknesses: Ceases within hours above the brine line, so every engagement she chooses has to happen near water
Stops below the spirit tier because the brine sac splits the penetrating vessel, which means nothing she knows will work on a cultivator who has reached further
Carries no qi reserve and no technique that answers a direct assault
Has spent a decade producing a series that is measurably less trustworthy than the first, and knows it
reference_stats.combat_read: Get her away from the water and the fight is already won, because she does not weaken so much as stop. On her ground she is close to immovable: stand still on her, crowd her, and let the brine do the work, because a body built for concentration has no answer to something that simply keeps arriving. Anything requiring a held breath or a stored reserve fails against her, and anything fast beats her easily until the water is involved.
notes: The tallies of her own recalibrations are cut into the instrument pole, so the record of her error travels with the thing that produced it.
Her first survey is the only series taken against the standing weight and it is the only one nobody has had to reconcile.

art.palette_notes: Wet slate and brine green with bleached bone highlights, and a single red-dyed cord on the instrument case as the only warm accent in the frame. Everything is reflective: the oilskin, the standing water, the gauge rim, so the light comes back off three surfaces before it reaches the face. Linework is thin and confident, drawn the way an instrument scale is drawn.

identity.realm: No path taken. A deepsalt taken above the brine line does not become ill; it simply stops, and the whole of his trade happens at the line

appearance.presentation: A broad, slow, damp man who never leaves the wet shelf of a pass and is never once mistaken for a traveller. He carries a clerk's satchel under water most of the day and has the bearing of somebody waiting for an instruction that will not arrive.
appearance.age: Old for the saturated floor and young enough that the second generation of the famine is still his responsibility. A deepsalt is brittle until its second year and he was not.
appearance.build: Heavy and broad, the hardest frame in a lineage already built for load, with a low centre of gravity that makes him difficult to shift.
appearance.complexion: Waxy grey-brown, permanently wet, and visibly drying in any moving air, which is why he is always slightly damp and never quite comfortable.
appearance.hair: Coarse black, wet and heavy, cut short at the nape and left alone otherwise because hair is a thing that dries and he is a thing that does not.
appearance.eyes: Small, deep-set and pale, and given to fixing on a single ledger line for a long time without appearing to read any of the rest.
appearance.palette: Brine green, wet umber and heavy lead grey, with the writ house's bone-white shoulder cord as the only value he did not choose.
appearance.attire: A heavy canvas apron over oilskin, sealed at the neck and the wrist with waxed cord, and boots cut away at the instep for standing water. Everything is designed to be worn while submerged and none of it is designed to dry.
appearance.marks: A pale mineral bloom across the shoulders where the brine sits longest, and a rope burn on both forearms from carrying a satchel that is always heavier than a satchel should be.
appearance.bearing: Immobile in the way a boulder is immobile, and profoundly uncomfortable anywhere his skin is drying.

canon.role_in_story: The jade writ's clerk on the one pass that crosses the ridge, and the only officer on it who can reach the sill without leaving the wet shelf. A population crossed the stair and neither arrived nor sent word, so the departure roll has no arrival column and the fee total never nets out. He entered an arrival for one name to close a single crossing, because a house cannot hold a debt that cannot be collected and a fee that never nets out is the reason a debt house exists. He has never seen the body and cannot produce it.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at the sill with the arrival column open in front of him and one name already written in his own hand, having just written it, while the crossing behind him is still in the act of happening.
canon.lore: Passage is the only supply chain in the setting whose unit is a person, because the cost of existing rises about fortyfold per tier and only a body can be moved, so permission to pass is the one thing anyone can actually control between tiers. Nobody may levy a seat, which is the central prohibition in the passage ledger and the reason a marshal's authority exists at all. A body arriving where a group it relied on is unwritten is injured rather than slowed, because a world boundary is not a wall but the edge of a law budget, so the only scarce thing at a crossing is a person the far side will not reject. A deepsalt is the saltfolk of the saturated basin floor, specialised past the parent body until the brine stops being a habitat and becomes a requirement, and above the line it simply stops within hours.
history: Born on the saturated floor of the basin and raised in a lineage that could not use the pan organisms its parent ate.
Took the writ's sill post because it is the only wage on the ridge that can be worked standing in water for a whole shift.
Kept the arrival column for six crossings and found nothing to enter, because the stair takes people out of this world and does not reliably return them.

Entered one arrival on a season when the fee would not reconcile, using a name from the departure roll and a body he had not seen, because a closed crossing clears a held fee and an unclosed one is uncollectable.
Been asked twice since which arrival he was writing from memory and has answered both times from the roll.

personality.summary: Placid, unhurried and incurably literal, with a talent for holding a rule exactly as written. He believes he has done the office a service, would say so if asked, and has not yet understood that a balance is a statement about the world rather than about the book.
traits: keeps a column the way other people keep a grudge, and it is not a grudge
will not enter anything he has not seen the body for, having entered exactly one exception
treats a fee that reconciles as a job done well
says the same thing the same way every time, including the parts he would rather leave out
cannot leave the wet shelf and does not resent it, because he has never been on the dry side long enough to compare
mannerisms: wipes the satchel rim with a wet thumb before opening it
counts the entries twice, aloud, before he rules the line
plants both feet and does not shift while he is being shouted at
answers a question by finishing the sentence the rule begins
rolls his sleeves above the elbow before wading, and never puts them down again while on shift
motivations: wants the crossing to reconcile again and knows, in the part of him that runs on rhythm, that it reconciled for the wrong reason
wants the arrival he wrote confirmed by anything at all, including a body
wants somebody above him to read the column rather than the balance
wants to be told that closing a fee is not the same as closing a crossing
flaws: wrote an arrival he had no observation for and reported it as an observation
cannot conceive of a rule as an instrument of concealment, only as an obstacle to accuracy
has never left the wet shelf and therefore has no idea what he is preventing
answers questions about that one arrival from the roll rather than from himself, and does it smoothly
personality.voice: Slow, plain and entirely without emphasis, the voice of a man reading a rule aloud. He states consequences as arithmetic and never as accusations, and the flatness has never once been mistaken for hostility.
taboos: will not enter a name in any column he has not watched being written
will not leave the wet shelf while on shift, whatever is said to him
refuses to strike the arrival he wrote, because striking it would leave the fee uncollected
will not speculate aloud about where a departed body went

relationships.note: Departure rolls with no arrival column, a fee total that never nets out, and no message in either direction. He wrote one arrival so that one crossing would reconcile, and the settlement test the mystery asks for is one body from the roll alive or one arrival record naming somebody not on it. His is the second kind, and he does not know that it is the settlement.

The office collects debts of access rather than money at the one pass that crosses the ridge, because passage is the only supply chain whose unit is a person and somebody has to decide who is owed the gate. It pays him by the hour to stand in water, which is the cheapest possible way to own a column that never balances.

The Watch is paid out of the ring's take at the foot of the stair and exists because a queue of bodies must not become a fight. It holds the other end of the movement that empties his column, and the two offices have never added their figures up, because neither reads the other's column.

Above the brine line a deepsalt stops within hours rather than becoming ill, which is what makes the sill post the only work he can hold and the only reason he has never seen a crossing from the far side. He cannot follow any of the people he has written into that column.

The levy roll grows and nothing on it closes because a levy that cannot be closed never needs closing. His arrival column and that roll are the walked gap entered in two registers, and the discovery that would settle either one would settle both.

The ledger records a central prohibition, that a seat may not be levied, and records nothing about the last time somebody levied one. A prohibition with no recorded violation is a prohibition with no enforcement, and Quist is the first man in four centuries to have quietly broken the rule the crossing is built on, by making one passage look completed.

That body's authority over the crossings descends from the prohibition itself and would descend from a refusal instead if one had ever been recorded. There has never been one, so the office that would audit Quist's column is standing on four centuries of nothing.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot be dragged out of water and cannot be hurt much by anything that has to land accurately. Fights as a fixed obstacle with a ledger under one arm. Treat him as a body you must displace rather than a body you must defeat, and note that displacement is the one thing in this setting he cannot survive at all.
strengths: The hardest frame in a lineage built for load, which means he does not get moved by anything of his own weight
Reads a sill and a submerged ledge in the dark by touch and by pressure, so he works a crossing at night better than anyone who can see
Cannot be shaken, flattened or impressed, because nothing in his trade is a threat
Knows the only pass on the ridge in enough detail to be trusted with a column that matters
weaknesses: Above the brine line he stops within hours, so every fight he is in has to be fought standing in water
Carries no technique of any kind and no path, so nothing he does scales against anything
Ceases at a salt ceiling far below anything he would meet on a pass, so a cultivator arriving from the far side outclasses him absolutely
His usefulness depends entirely on nobody reading his column closely, which is the standing he has now destroyed for himself
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not fight him in water; take the water away. He is effectively invulnerable on his own ground and completely defenceless anywhere else, and the transition between the two is measured in hours rather than seconds, so the whole engagement is a problem of positioning rather than of force. Anything with reach is decisive once he is out of the channel, and anything that cannot leave the water will get exactly as tired as he is and then a little more.
notes: He has never been on the far side of the sill, so the setting's one person who writes arrivals has never seen an arrival.
The exception he made is not recorded anywhere as an exception, which is the reason it has never been found.

identity.realm: Mind path, Insight gate; a marshfolk pools qi low and wide in a broad pelvic basin and takes it from wet ground efficiently and dry ground poorly

appearance.presentation: A broad, soft, web-footed woman with permanently damp skin and a permanent expression of listening to something under the floor. She keeps a roll at her hip and treats it the way other people treat a child.
appearance.age: Middle for her kind and old for a queue. A marshfolk's infancy is timed to the water and hers was not, and she has the flat feet of somebody who has walked dry ground her whole life and resents it.
appearance.build: Soft, heavy and low, with a long prehensile tail-prop she uses for balance on stairs and otherwise forgets she has.
appearance.complexion: Damp grey-pink, drying to flaky patches in any heated room, and she is always sitting nearer the door for the draught.
appearance.hair: Wet-dark, worn in a thick braid pinned flat against the skull so it will not catch on a helmet strap.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set, gold-rimmed and slightly protruding, adapted to see a silted bottom rather than a face, and never quite settling on a person at close range.
appearance.palette: Reed brown, silt green, and a dull watch-brass shoulder plate, with the pale chalk of a duty roster as the only high value in her kit.
appearance.attire: A heavy canvas queue coat cut short at the hip so the tail-prop clears it, sleeves bound above the wrist, and cut-away boots that will never fully dry. She wears the watch plate on one shoulder only, because the other one carries the roll.
appearance.marks: A band of dry-scalded skin around both ankles where a marshfolk's body has been kept out of water too long, and a bruise-coloured mark on the tail-prop root from a stair rail.
appearance.bearing: Slightly crouched, weight on the balls of her feet, tail-prop trailing for balance. She stands where she can feel the floor's vibration and turns her head toward anything moving underfoot before she looks up.

canon.role_in_story: The levy roll keeper at the foot of the stair, and the only officer whose pay scales with the size of a roll that never closes. A levy company is paid per name and keeps a roll of people who were levied and neither returned nor were recorded dead, so the roll grows and nothing on it closes. She struck one name off it to make a period balance, using a process that does not first require the roll to shrink, which is precisely the settlement the roll has been waiting four centuries for and which nobody will now believe.
canon.first_appearance: First seen crouching at the foot of the stair with a chalked roster board across her knees and a name rubbed out on it, asking a queue-runner whether a levy is considered recovered when nobody ever goes and looks for the body.
canon.lore: A marshfolk is a wading amphibian lineage that breathes air and nests on floating mats, so it is neither one parent nor the other but the body in between: a three-point stance distributed over splayed toes and a tail-prop, which never loads a heel, which is why the two heel vessels never form and the fourteenth gate is the wall. The only standing force on the plains is posted at the foot of the stair and paid out of the ring's take, and it exists because the one door out of a world that licenses nobody to enter it fills with unlicensed arrivals, and a queue of bodies is the one thing that must not become a fight. Its other line item is a levy roll with no closure column, which is the walked gap entered in the wrong register, and the two have never been added up because neither office reads the other's column.
history: Hatched on a reed mat in a floodplain margin and carried under a brood pouch through the dry season, which is the ordinary arrangement and which she has never forgiven.
Posted to the stair foot because a marshfolk feels a queue through standing water and through a floor, and the watch wanted somebody who could feel a crowd without looking at it.
Given the levy roll and the instruction that a period does not close while the roll is open, which she read as an instruction about periods.
Struck one name to make a period balance, using the settlement process that does not require the roll to shrink, and understood afterwards that this was the settlement the mystery asks for.
Been asked twice to produce the name back and has twice produced the closure instead, and has begun to suspect that this is why nobody asks a third time.

personality.summary: Burdensome, stubborn and extremely bad at saying the thing she means, with a memory for individuals that is the exact inverse of what her office requires. She likes people and the job is a list, and the collision has been resolved in favour of the list because the list pays.
traits: remembers every face that has ever passed her post and has to be talked out of saying so
counts compulsively and stops when she catches herself
refuses to call a levy recovered while the person is unlocated
is loyal past every point that would be sensible, to the post rather than to the office
cannot lie about a name, only about what has happened to it
mannerisms: crouches to write on a low board rather than bending, which she learned as a hatching reflex
turns her head toward the floor before she turns it toward a speaker
taps the roll twice with two fingers before she agrees to anything
uses her tail-prop for balance on stairs without being aware of doing it
goes very quiet in a crowd, because a crowd is louder to her than it looks
motivations: wants the struck name struck again and put back, and cannot find a process that will allow it
wants the closure to be disbelieved so that somebody reopens the roll properly
wants one name off that roll to come back alive, so that the strike stops being a rumour
wants to stop being the person a queue tells things to
flaws: used the one process that settles the roll and could not be undone, on a name she had never met
keeps a private count of the faces against the roll's count of names, and the two do not agree
is more attached to individuals than the office can survive and would sabotage a levy to keep one alive
believes a settled question is a solved question, and acted on it
personality.voice: Warm, low and unhurried, and slower than the room expects. She talks about people when the question is about entries, and it takes a second question to get the entry.
taboos: will not call a levy recovered while the person is unlocated
will not write a name she has not heard said aloud in this season
refuses to burn a roster board, having seen what a burned board costs later
will not answer a question about a struck name with anything but the closure that struck it

relationships.note: The roll grows and nothing on it closes, and the settlement test is one name struck by a process that does not first require the roll to shrink. She used exactly that process to make a period balance, which is why the mystery now has a settlement nobody can act on twice.

The only standing force on the plains, paid out of the ring's take and posted where a queue must not become a fight. Its pay scales with the size of an open roll rather than with any recovery, so the officer who keeps the roll has never had a reason to close it and now cannot.

That people count a life by how many of the realm's gates were already closed when they were born, which is the setting's asymptote: the whole ladder arrives late by definition. Every name on her roll is somebody who went up and did not come back down, and the roll is the only institution that has counted them.

Departure rolls with no arrival column, a fee total that never nets out, and no message in either direction. Her roll and that column are the same missing people written in two offices' books, and the discovery that would settle either would settle both.

The three-point stance never loads a heel, so the two heel vessels cannot form and the fourteenth gate is the wall, which puts every levy she has ever collected far above anything she can reach. She feels a crowd through the floor and cannot feel a person she is not touching, which is why the strike was the only option she had.

That office collects debts of access at the one pass and holds a crossing fee that never nets out. Between them the two offices hold both columns of the same gap, and four centuries of nobody adding them up is the standing order they were both built on.

Cultivators walked up to the Spirit Peaks for spirit stone and did not come back, and the movement was economic before it was spiritual. Every line on her roll is a household that paid for that movement, and the roll is the only thing that ever came back with the receipts.

reference_stats.summary: A soft amphibian frame that cannot stand still and cannot load a heel, so nothing she does has leverage and nothing aimed at a standing target lands. Fights low, fast and in company. Treat her as something that has to be swept up rather than defeated, and note that a queue is her only real tactical asset.
strengths: Feels vibration through standing water and through a floor, so she knows the size and direction of a crowd before she looks at it
Three-point stance and a tail-prop make her almost impossible to put down once she is moving and trivial to pin once she is not
Takes qi out of wet ground efficiently and dry ground poorly, so the ground she chooses decides the engagement
Remembers every individual that has passed her post, which in a levy office is a strategic resource nobody has taught anyone to use
weaknesses: Stops at the fourteenth gate because the heel vessels never form, so anything cultivated well above her tier simply outclasses her
No heel to stand on and soft tissue throughout, so she is helpless against mineral bodies and anything that pins
Desiccates fast out of water, so every fight she picks has to happen near standing water or she dies in minutes
Carries a roll she reads too well, and would lose a fight to save a name on it
reference_stats.combat_read: Never let her set her feet; a marshfolk without somewhere to stand is a marshfolk on the floor, and a tail-prop is a handle. Force her toward dry ground and the engagement ends before it starts, because she cannot take qi out of it. Otherwise crowd her, keep her moving, and remember that the only thing in the field more dangerous than her is a queue she has decided to interpose herself for.
notes: Her private count of faces against the roll's count of names does not agree, and she has never been asked to reconcile them.
Nothing in a levy office is designed for an officer who remembers the people rather than the entries.

identity.realm: Mind path, Comprehension gate; a brinecaller is slow in either parent's own medium, which is the crossing's actual cost

appearance.presentation: A weather-beaten, narrow woman with salt on one side of her and water on the other and no instinct at all for which is which. She is the setting's best chemical nose and has spent forty years applying it to a problem it cannot smell.
appearance.age: Late for a crossing, which is not late, and old enough to remember when the school taught the other thing.
appearance.build: A saltfolk frame with a shallower sac and a tidecaller's frame overlaid on it, gracile and broad-handed, built for neither shore and comfortable on both.
appearance.complexion: Weathered and faintly salt-bloomed along one jaw, with the other half of the face permanently damp, so the two halves of her never quite match each other.
appearance.hair: Dark, brittle at the ends, worn in a school-cut braid with a strip of bleached cloth threaded through it that may or may not be a rank marker.
appearance.eyes: Narrow, deep-set and grey, and given to narrowing further when a claim is being made that chemistry cannot confirm.
appearance.palette: Bleached grey-green, tar black, and one band of pale salt-white at the collar, with a diff-frame of lacquered dark wood as the only furniture in her kit.
appearance.attire: A salt-cured coat over a woven underlayer, sleeves cut away entirely so the salt and the water on her skin are both visible, and flat-soled shoes resoled with tarred cord. She wears a school's grey cloak and has let it go the colour of everything she has washed it in.
appearance.marks: Split, salt-cracked skin across both knuckles, and a pale band across the throat where a colony strain's compatibility burn has been left untreated for years.
appearance.bearing: Leans slightly downhill, as though permanently standing on a shore that is not level, and turns her whole body to face a smell rather than a speaker.

canon.role_in_story: The second operator of the sixth-seat diff and the only person alive who knows the frame on which the form-only claim could be tested. The immortal tier holds four duplicate seats, which is exactly the surplus a diff needs, and a spare seat is not capacity for a new path, it is the only condition under which a law can be studied instead of obeyed. She ran the test, filed the result nowhere, and has spent four decades teaching the claim as a heresy from a school whose standing requires it to be one.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at the edge of a lecture floor with a lacquered diff-frame under one arm, explaining to a student that the claim their school teaches as a heresy was never tested in any frame the setting could build, while holding the only object in the building that would contradict her.
canon.lore: A tier's composition is learned by seating the last missing law, diffing what the tier newly permits, and arguing about which result caused the other; the finding worth recording is negative, because a spare seat buys observation rather than new paths, and that is the whole reason the highest tier is the one a mind occupies. The form-only reading is that migrating Body Dao becomes a school where form wins with physical law alone where qi is already spent, and it was recorded as a heresy because nothing in a three-slot frame can test it. An unwritten law does not merely restrict practice, it invents one. The method was commissioned by an order that is not named, kept both readings privately, and its one useful finding is known to everybody while the commission is known to nobody.
history: Born on a shoreline where both parent chemistries were reachable, which is the only place a crossing can happen and the reason the crossing spread along trade routes rather than across them.
Learned to tell two kinds of water apart at a glance, which is the best chemical sense in the record by a wide margin and is useless against a question about law.
Taught at the gap school, which seats a law, diffs what the tier newly permits, and moves the student somewhere that law is missing.
Was sent to the immortal tier with a diff-frame on a commission whose order is not named, and found four duplicate seats where the test was possible.
Ran the test, kept the result, and told nobody, because whichever reading lost was signed by the office that had to live beside the winner; she has taught the claim as untested ever since.

personality.summary: Precise, unpleasantly honest and quietly corrosive to her own institution, with a discipline built out of taking things apart and a temperament that cannot leave a finding alone. She has made herself the setting's only custodian of a suppressed result, and she pays for it in the currency she values most, which is being believed.
traits: names the objection before her opponent has finished making it
will not teach a claim she has tested and found wanting, and has taught one she has not
keeps a lacquered frame she will not lend and has never opened in company
reads a room by smell and is embarrassed about how much she uses it
answers a question about what is taught with what is known, in that order, every time
mannerisms: leans downhill even on level floors, from a lifetime of shorelines
takes a diffuse-frame out and turns it in her hands whenever a claim about a spare seat comes up
sniffs once, deliberately, before agreeing with anything
splits her answers into what was measured and what was decided, always in that order
sits with her back to a wall and her sleeves pushed up so both forearms are visible
motivations: wants the result entered somewhere it cannot be quietly lost, by a party with no claim on it
wants to be wrong, has looked for eleven ways to be, and has found the result unchanged by all of them
wants the order that commissioned the diff named, because a commission is the only thing that makes two readings the same finding
wants to stop teaching a sentence she has read the other side of
flaws: withheld the one result that would have changed her school's standing, on reasoning that was sound and entirely self-serving
cannot say the sentence out loud and has therefore told it four decades late
treats the diff-frame as a possession rather than as evidence, which is the habit the commission existed to break
has become the reason a tested heresy is still an untested one
personality.voice: Dry, precise and fast, with a habit of conceding a point so thoroughly that it functions as an attack. She uses her subject's own vocabulary and never simplifies it, which her students find either clarifying or insulting depending on the day.
taboos: will not call a claim untested in front of a student who could test it
refuses to lend the diff-frame to anyone, including the office that commissioned it
will not put a finding in a book she has not personally seen written down
will not teach the form-only claim as a heresy while the frame is in her possession

relationships.note: The immortal frame holds four duplicate seats, which is exactly the surplus a diff needs, so somewhere the form-only test was possible. She found where, ran it, and filed the result in neither. The absence of a result is the most stable fact about the claim, and she is the reason it is stable.

The diff that produced the setting's one useful finding kept both readings and kept them privately, and the order that commissioned it is not named. She was the second operator, so she knows which reading was removed and which survived, and she has never said so to the office that would have to live beside the answer.

The school teaches by seating a law, diffing what the tier newly permits, and moving the student somewhere that law is missing, because a spare seat is the only condition under which a law can be studied instead of obeyed. She teaches there, which is what makes her the living contradiction in its curriculum rather than merely a critic of it.

That claim is what migrating body practice becomes where qi is already spent, and it invents a discipline rather than merely restricting one. She has eleven attempts at refuting it on record and the claim has survived every one, which is why she teaches it as settled and does not believe she is lying.

A brinecaller reads two chemistries at once and is never native anywhere, because it needs both parents' water within reach and a shoreline is a contested piece of ground. The best chemical sense in the record is on a body whose entire life has been spent between two places it could not stay, which is also why she is the right person to hold a finding that belongs to neither side.

That mortal office certifies a breakthrough at the Cairn Field and is paid out of the gate fees, and it needs the top tier's slack to read as design, because an inherited surplus is an accident somebody else made. If her result were filed, the seat's whole standing would rest on which reading was removed, and she has decided that is not hers to hand over.

The slack reading is the setting's most useful sentence and the entire reason a mind occupies the highest tier. She has taught it every season for four decades and cannot stop teaching it, because the reading is true and the test she ran would make it true in a way the tier's stewards cannot survive.

reference_stats.summary: Carries a body that reads two chemistries at once and belongs to no shore, so her senses are the best in the setting and her frame is nobody's home. Fights as a reader who has to be at close range to do it. Treat her as someone who will know what you are standing in before you do and who has no answer at all once you are on top of her.
strengths: The best chemical sense in the record by a wide margin, and always being lied to by one of the two chemistries she reads
Tolerates brine and fresh water alike, so no poison, brine, solvent or alchemical agent lands as a surprise on her
Reads a diff frame faster than anyone who has to think about what a spare seat is for
Structurally neither parent, so no faction, household or school's own claim on her is automatic
weaknesses: Ceases at a salt-line wall far below the tier she tested, so any opponent cultivated past it is out of her class entirely
Slower in both parents' own mediums than either parent is, which is the crossing's actual cost and shows in every fight
No reservoir and no technique that rewards distance, so a determined fast body ends her before she reads anything
Would rather be doubted than complicit, which makes her trivially easy to discredit and impossible to buy
reference_stats.combat_read: Get close, because everything she is worth happens at arm's length and everything she is worth disappears at range. Bring a weapon that leaves something behind, since a reading is only half of her advantage and the other half is knowing what to do about it. Do not fight her on a shoreline you chose: she is never native anywhere, and a body that is comfortable everywhere is a body that has been uncomfortable everywhere and knows it.
notes: She carries a lacquered diff frame she will not lend and has never opened in company, which is the closest thing to a confession the setting has.
The claim she teaches as untested has survived eleven attempts of hers at refuting it, which is a stronger record than the school will print.
