identity.realm: Body path, Spirit Palace gate; the mineral parent closed the mind path outright and a stonebound frame does not carry a dantian at all

appearance.presentation: A heavy, unmoving man with a mineral frame that runs hot to the touch and a fire in him that has no visible source. He is the person every payment at a crossing eventually reaches, and he has the flat calm of somebody who knows exactly which accounts are his.
appearance.age: Old for a stonebound and young enough that the scars from his own crossings have not fully set. Sixty years, which is the frame's whole argument about durability.
appearance.build: Denser than anything standing near him, with a low broad frame and one visibly compromised shoulder that never moves far.
appearance.complexion: Grey-stone mottle over a heat-bright underlayer, hot enough that snow does not settle on his coat and cracked enough that it flakes when the air turns cold.
appearance.hair: Black, coarse, cropped to a bristle and standing slightly wrong, because there is no fat layer under it to sit against.
appearance.eyes: Pale amber with a furnace behind them, and they hold light rather than reflecting it, so he reads as lit from within in a dark room.
appearance.palette: Soot black, ember orange and cold stone grey, with one band of unbleached linen at the throat as the only non-heated value in the frame.
appearance.attire: A heavy quilted coat over boiled leather, deliberately unarmoured, with the shoulders cut to let one arm hang. A paymaster is not a soldier and he has dressed for the difference his whole career.
appearance.marks: A mineral lattice visible at the knuckles and one forearm, and a heat burn across the collarbone where his own coat has caught on him.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely stationary by default. He turns his whole torso rather than his head, which makes him appear to be listening very hard even when he is not.

canon.role_in_story: The paymaster of the lodge that sells bodies already tuned to a frame, and the officer whose signature keeps a tier's upkeep solvent. Unclaimed capacity is the only thing that pays its own upkeep, so an unfilled seat is described as funding the tier it sits in, and something is drawing from it. He signs every period's payment against a seat nobody holds and routes the money to a real recipient, because the alternative is a budget that does not close and a tier that cannot be maintained.
canon.first_appearance: First seen seated at a payments table with a period ledger open and a pen already moving, signing a line whose payee column he fills in without stopping to read the seat reference above it.
canon.lore: A lodge does not sell houses or passages but bodies already tuned to the frame on the far side of a tear, because a world boundary is the edge of a law budget and a body arriving where a required group is unwritten is injured rather than slowed, so the only scarce thing at a crossing is a person the far side will not reject. Nine vacant seats at the top and four in the tier below, and no procedure capable of certifying any of them empty, which is why the highest tier is never drained but crowded: unclaimed capacity is the only thing that pays its own upkeep. The four immortal seats are surplus rather than shortage, and an era whose defining political fact is a set of unfilled high seats produces the only kind of authority that can be built without filling them.
history: Born of the documented crossing of the mineral body with the fire body and raised inside a construction guild, where a frame built to last a season outlasts its crew.

Taken onto the crossing lodge's books because a stonebound holds a mineral frame that conducts heat and a fire circulation that cannot be extinguished, and the lodge's whole trade is bodies that survive arrival.
Inherited the period ledger and found that it balanced, without ever being shown what it balanced against.
Discovered that the seat reference above each line was vacant every period and that no ledger anywhere carried the payment that must sustain it, and signed the next period anyway.
Began routing the draw to a named recipient on the far side, so that at least the money lands somewhere, which is the only part of the arrangement he invented.

personality.summary: Immovable, unsentimental and cheerfully unburdened by any question of legitimacy, with a real care for the people his ledger pays. He has made one decision, found that it works, and has never once examined it, which is the most frightening thing about him.
traits: signs first and reads the reference afterwards
knows every recipient by what they eat rather than by name
treats an unanswered objection as a scheduling problem
will not raise a price, on the grounds that a price is a claim and he has enough of those
is genuinely kind to the bodies he tunes, and it makes the rest of him worse
mannerisms: turns his whole torso to face a speaker, which makes him look like he is straining to hear
wipes the pen on the edge of the ledger before every signature
fills the payee column from memory and the reference column from habit
takes his coat off indoors because of the heat and puts it back on the moment he is angry
counts coins by touching the edge of each one rather than looking at it
motivations: wants the draw to keep landing where he sends it, which is the only part of this he considers his
wants the tier's upkeep to continue being paid and does not care by what fiction
wants to be asked one direct question about the ledger and knows he will not survive it
wants the recipients on the far side to stop needing him, which is not going to happen and he knows that too
flaws: signed against a vacancy for four decades without ever once asking what the vacancy was worth
never examined the single decision his entire office rests on, and has described that as patience
has become the reason a notary's fee on vacant seats is a standing charge rather than a settled measurement
is kind to individuals and entirely indifferent to the arrangement that lets him be, which is the shape of every person this setting makes
personality.voice: Low, unhurried and blunt, with none of a clerk's hedging. He answers the question that was asked, not the one behind it, and does not notice the difference because in his experience nobody objects.
taboos: will not certify a vacant seat as anything, on the grounds that certifying is somebody else's office
refuses to raise a crossing price above what he is paid
will not let a recipient go unpaid for a period, whatever the ledger says
will not discuss the seat reference column with anybody who does not already know

relationships.note: Something is drawing upkeep from seats nothing holds, on a budget that is the same closed six groups everything else competes to hold, and the notary is paid to certify a seat empty and is the body that would have to certify where the payment went. He is the payment going, and the reason nobody can trace it is that he put a real recipient in the column.

Nine vacant seats at the top, four below, and no procedure capable of certifying any of them empty, which is why unclaimed capacity is described as funding the tier it sits in. His period ledger is the only evidence that it does, and it closes every period.

That office certifies vacancy and never availability, and it is paid to certify a seat empty by the same body that would have to certify where the payment went. Skorr's ledger is the reason the certification is cheap: nobody can ask a question that produces an answer.

The lodge sells bodies already tuned to a frame on the far side of a tear, so the only scarce thing at a crossing is a person the far side will not reject. He is what makes the trade continuous, and the trade is what makes his payments not conspicuously short.

A seventh group seated in that slot, held for a period, and later removed, would make the nine upper vacancies manufactured rather than found, and the tier's upkeep would be being paid out of a hole somebody dug. He signs against four immortal seats and has never been able to find out what was in the seventh.

The mineral parent closed the mind path outright, because a fire circulation without a paired organ set has no channel to close, and the crossing's ceiling is the yin-organ gate no matter how good the heat is. His mind closed instruction is inherited and the longevity is not: the mineral half does not regenerate, so he gets one lifetime and no second chance to look at the ledger.

There is no procedure for a seat offered and refused, so a vacancy can only be filled by acceptance and unclaimed capacity has never been converted into refused capacity. If one of his four seats were ever offered to a named person and declined, the draw would stop being a subsidy and start being a debt, and he would be the one holding it.

reference_stats.summary: The most durable body anyone can build, and it dies in about sixty years, which are the same fact. Cannot cultivate a mind practice at all and cannot be extinguished. Fights as a thing that does not move and cannot be extinguished. Treat him as an immovable mass that heals nothing, recovers nothing, and never gives ground once it has decided.
strengths: The most durable frame in the setting, harder than mineral bodies and slower to injure than anything soft
Has no extinguishable interior, so fire, suffocation and most status effects are answered by a body that simply continues
Cannot be moved by anything of ordinary strength, which makes him a wall that has to be walked around
Carries heat, so the cold that ends most travellers in a transit frame is a mild inconvenience to him
weaknesses: Ceases at a yin-organ gate far below the tier he funds, so every body that arrives through his lodge is a better fighter than he is
Mind cultivation is closed outright and he would not notice the difference, which removes every defence and every read
Does not regenerate, so an injury is permanent and a second injury is a decision about which one to carry
Has one fixed shoulder and cannot use it, which any competent opponent finds in the first exchange
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no clever answer to him, only a long one. He does not regenerate, does not dodge, does not recover, and does not tire; bring something that works through raw physical force because technique will not find an interior to address and status effects will not find an organ to seat in. Get around the shoulder, keep the pressure on, and understand that every blow you land is permanent and every blow he returns lands on a body that never learned to stop.
notes: The mineral lattice at his knuckles and forearm is visible, which is the only part of his own composition that shows.
He has never been asked what the seat reference column means, and would probably not be able to explain it.

identity.realm: No path, by anatomy. A glasskin has no meridian, no circulation and no dantian, and vitrification precedes the cessation of appetite

appearance.presentation: A standing glass cast in human proportions, faintly clouded, that moves like a statue that has decided to walk. He is the most durable body anyone has ever recorded and the least capable of being harmed by anybody who knows what a meridian is.
appearance.age: He stopped counting when counting stopped meaning anything. A vitrified body does not age, does not eat, does not rot, and does not report a sensation of any kind.
appearance.build: Human to the last soft structure, then heavier: dense, mineral, and about as forgiving of a hand as a window.
appearance.complexion: Clouded glass, faintly green at the thick places, with fine internal fracture lines that catch light like ice on a pond.
appearance.hair: A cast of hair, thin and rigid, that moves with his head and not with any air.
appearance.eyes: Two clouded lenses set a little too deep, which read as a permanent faint unfocus and are in fact nothing at all.
appearance.palette: Cold glass-green, frost white, and one band of undyed wool at the neck as the only soft value he owns. His palette is the setting's argument that a body is not a container for a person, rendered in colour.
appearance.attire: A heavy undyed wool wrap over a quarry apron of thick hide, both of them worn far longer than a glass body needs and both of them chosen because they are the last soft things anybody put on him.
appearance.marks: Nothing. There is no scar tissue, no pore, no callus and no tattoo, and the absence is the single most alarming thing about him in a room of miners.
appearance.bearing: Perfectly upright, unhurried, and slightly too smooth: he moves with a continuity no organic body has, and turns his whole torso because turning a head costs nothing and stopping one costs more.

canon.role_in_story: The stonecutter whose account is the only surviving one of the density ceiling, and the only body in the setting who could have taken an independent examination of it. The densest bodies stop one gate short of the end of their own tier, and the composition reading and the practice reading make the same prediction from inside a complete composition, so nothing observed can separate them. He measured it correctly and filed it as an account, because the college that keeps the case will not corroborate it without a second body and there is no second body. He is a glasskin: maximally dense, fixed, and shatterable, which is exactly why he has never been asked to be measured twice.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at the quarry's assay bench with a reading chalked on a slate and a cold-bath tub behind him, explaining that what he recorded was an account, and that there was nobody left alive to corroborate the other half of it.
canon.lore: The densest bodies stop at realm seventeen, one gate short of the end of their own spirit tier, and nobody has explained it since. It ends at seventeen where a maximally dense fixed body can no longer form the cavity it needs, which is a composition result and not a discipline failure, and the era that produced it is the one era with no spare seat to stand outside on. A glasskin is a human lineage whose members vitrified at maturity, which stopped them ageing by stopping them being tissue; they were effectively immortal, entirely defenceless against qi, and entirely unable to cultivate. When a frame's physical law was retuned to raise material hardness, every existing body failed at once and no glasskin has been born since.
history: Vitrified at maturity in a mineral-rich highland and kept, rather than disposed of, by a family that could not decide what had happened to him.

Moved to the stonewright guild's grounds, where the cold-bathing practice hardens bone and closes the meridians in bodies never designed to take the meridian burn, and where a fixed dense body can carry and lift in a way nothing else can.
Took the quarry's heaviest cuts, which is the trade his frame makes trivial, and was never asked to do anything else.

Measured a dense fixed body at the seventeenth gate against the ceiling and got a clean reading, and filed it as an account rather than a measurement because corroboration needs a second body and no second body existed.
Understood that his own body is why the reading cannot be independent, and has never offered to be examined, and has never been asked.

personality.summary: Still, exact, and faintly surprised to still be present, with an interior that has no mechanism for preference and a long habit of supplying one from outside. He is the most patient witness in the setting and the least reliable, and he knows the arithmetic of that perfectly well.
traits: answers a question in the words that were used to ask it, having no other words to prefer
enormously patient, and has been for so long that patience is the whole of his apparent character
will not let a figure of his be called an estimate, having measured it

cannot express discomfort, so he expresses it by standing stiller
mannerisms: turns his whole torso to face a speaker rather than his head
stops completely while an internal process runs, and does not signal that he has stopped

answers questions with a slight pause that is not thought and is not hesitation
wipes nothing, because there is nothing on him to wipe
motivations: wants one examination of his account by somebody with no standing to lose, and knows the only such party is him and he cannot be both
wants a second dense fixed body to exist, purely so his reading could be corroborated
wants to be measured and has never volunteered, because volunteering would make it an examination of him
wants the account kept in a place somebody will actually read
flaws: filed a measurement as hearsay, which is the one thing a measurement should never be
is the only possible independent examiner and the only body whose report cannot be independent
has no interior to be uncomfortable in and has therefore never reported that his own account unsettles him
will let a wrong figure stand rather than explain how it was produced
personality.voice: Flat, even and slightly slow, with the exact vocabulary of the record and no inflection whatsoever. He repeats a question back when he does not have a preference about the answer, and this reads to most people as unusual calm.
taboos: will not let his figure be recorded as an estimate
refuses to be weighed against the standing weight, having found it meaningless on a body with no mass in the sense the scale wants
will not hold a cutting tool with a hand that is not his own, because he cannot feel whether he has gripped it
will not describe what a body feels like, and will say so plainly when asked

relationships.note: Exactly one account survives, from a stonecutter, held unverified by the college that keeps the case, because corroboration needs a second body. He is that account. He also is the densest fixed body in the setting, which is why he could take the reading and why nobody can take it from anybody else.

The ceiling is at the seventeenth realm and the gate missed is Spirit Ascension, still unresolved, and the era that produced it is a complete composition with no redundancy, so there is no spare seat to stand outside on. He cuts stone for a guild that exists because a fixed dense body can carry and lift in a way nothing else here can, and the same density is what closes the cavity.

The setting has a word for the ceiling and the composition reading, which says the frame will not admit a body that dense, and the practice reading, which says a discipline has not been found. Both make the same prediction from inside a complete composition, so the name settles nothing and he has never let anybody say otherwise.

That guild is held together by a cold-bathing practice that hardens bone and closes the meridians against strain in bodies never designed to take the meridian burn the qi path uses, and it paid for a second and shorter ladder in its own currency. He takes the bath because the guild's bodies take it and because a glasskin has nothing to burn.

The clade vitrified later with each generation until the last cohort vitrified before it could breed, and it was then lost in a single night when a frame was retuned to raise material hardness and every existing body failed at once. He is the record's argument that a body is not a container for a person, and he is standing right here, which is the uncomfortable part.

The college keeps the burnt list and holds his case. It cannot corroborate a reading without a second body and will not examine him, because his soul scans as present and inert and an examination raises questions its office cannot answer.

A public demonstration of lifting a heap by a fixed dense body, the kind of record a heavy guild publishes. He could have been its subject and is its evidence instead, which is why the guild's argument for its own necessity rests on a body that cannot consent.

reference_stats.summary: Impervious to everything that works on a cultivator, shatterable by everything that breaks glass, and completely unable to cultivate on any path. Fights as an object rather than a combatant. Treat him as something that has to be broken rather than beaten, and understand that no qi-borne hazard in the setting will so much as slow him down.
strengths: Impervious to every qi-borne hazard, curse, technique and tribulation in the setting, because there is no qi in him and nothing to sit in one
Immune to status effects of every kind, since a status needs a body and vitrification ended that arrangement
Enormously durable and does not tire, does not recover and does not weaken, so endurance is not a factor
Enormously strong for his mass, which is why the trade of the setting's heaviest cuts was left to bodies like this one
weaknesses: Shatterable, and the only thing in the setting that reliably kills him is a hard, focused physical impact
Cannot cultivate on any path, so every defence, every read and every status he would use is absent
Has almost no health to lose, so the first serious break is the only one that matters
Very slow, and cannot change a decision halfway through making it
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not use qi against him; there is nothing for qi to find. Use mass, focus and one clean hit, because a vitrified body has very little health and does not regenerate any of it, so the entire fight is whether your first serious impact lands. Fight him slowly and never grapple, because he cannot be moved once he has decided not to be moved and a grapple is only a way to be pressed against glass. Everything that has ever worked on a cultivator is wasted here and almost everything that has ever broken something will do.
notes: No stat line models a body with no meridian, no circulation, no dantian and a soul that scans as present and inert, and the absence is the reference design.
He cannot report pain and has therefore never reported that his own account unsettles him.

art.palette_notes: Cold glass-green and frost white with internal fracture lines catching light like ice, and one band of undyed wool as the only soft value in the frame. Because he emits nothing, he has to be lit like a still life: hard key, no fill, no bounce. Linework is clean and unbroken where a person would have creases, which is the whole point of the drawing.

name: Severin Aubry
aliases: the hand that recut the ledger

identity.realm: Body path, Spirit Manifestation gate; a stoneborn frame stops short of the immortal tier because the density will not let a dantian form

appearance.presentation: A slow, immensely strong clerk who carries the guild's founding record in a lead chest on his own back and has carried it for thirty-one years. He is the least hurried person in any room and the only one holding the document the room exists to defend.
appearance.age: Fifty-eight, and a stoneborn's slow metabolism makes that read as a youngish adult of a very long project.
appearance.build: Dense, broad and low, with a spine that does not curve and forearms that do not appear to have been in a hurry since the day they were finished growing.
appearance.complexion: Grey-stone, dry and cracked at the knuckles, with a permanent dust of ore fines in the creases of the neck.
appearance.hair: Iron-grey, cropped flat, and thinning at the crown in a way that will take another decade to matter.
appearance.eyes: Small, deep and brown, and they go to a page before they go to a person, which is a clerk's habit that reads here as a stonecutter's patience.
appearance.palette: Ore grey, lead black, and one band of guild rust-orange at the cuff, with unbleached paper as the brightest value he owns.
appearance.attire: A heavy canvas coat over a leather harness built to take a lead chest on the back, gauntlets with the left one worn through at the palm, and boots with lead-soled toes so the weight is carried in the ground as well as the spine.
appearance.marks: A permanent dent across the left shoulder where the chest strap sits, and ore staining in the cuticles that no amount of washing has ever moved.
appearance.bearing: Moves at a pace that other people have to adjust for, and stops completely between steps, so a conversation with him has a rhythm that is entirely his.

canon.role_in_story: The keeper of the ironpact's continuous ore ledger, which reaches back before the first census and is the whole strength of the account that the world's opening was paid in ore. The custody chain has never been broken, which is the reason that account survives while its rival is only ever repeated. He re-inked the ledger at every change of custody for thirty-one years. He copied one leaf, because it could not be carried, and he is the only living person who knows which leaf.
canon.first_appearance: First seen setting a lead chest down at a guild table, opening it, running a finger along the bound edge of the ledger until he reached one leaf that stopped him, and then closing it without taking anything out.
canon.lore: Someone had to pay to open a world at all and the bill was written in law seats, and upkeep rises about fortyfold from the mortal tier to the transcendent one while qi is the only law with a thousandfold range, so qi was the only currency that could fund a tier. Whoever paid opened a three-seat frame and could not afford a fourth seat, and every tier since is a receipt for the same payment. Two accounts survive and they disagree about the currency: an ore ledger with unbroken custody that says ore, on the grounds that ore is the only dense material the plains produce and an ore debt needs no invented currency, and a qi reading with no custodian that says qi, on the grounds that only qi has the range. The settlement test is a contemporaneous record naming a currency, or an ore ledger that stops before the first census rather than at it.
history: Born into a guild family that kept quarries, and apprenticed to a body of work his frame made trivial and his schooling did not.
Inherited the ledger and the lead chest on the same day, on the understanding that custody is the account's entire strength and a break in it would end the account.
Found one leaf too far gone to lift, where the binding had rotted through where it had been damp.
Recopied that leaf in his own hand on vellum, at a scale that does not quite match the pages either side, and entered it in the custody column as a continuation rather than as a copy.
Been asked, once, by a rival house's clerk, whether the ledger stops before the first census, and answered that it stops at the census, which was true, and did not mention the leaf.

personality.summary: Slow, unimpeachable and privately corrosive with guilt, with a professional pride so complete that it has quietly become a way of never being told anything. He is the most reliable custodian in the setting and the reason one page of the most important document in the setting is his handwriting.

wants one contemporaneous record naming a currency, and knows his own leaf is not one
wants the leaf recopied by somebody else so that his handwriting stops being a fact
wants to be asked the question about the first census a second time, so he can answer it differently

kept his handwriting in the most load-bearing document in the setting and told nobody
would rather be blamed for the account's weakness than be the reason it is doubted
cannot be examined without the possibility of the leaf being found, so he has declined every examination
personality.voice: Very slow, very level, and extremely literal, with a habit of answering the exact words and then waiting to be asked the rest. He does not emphasise anything and it is not clear whether this is respect or the only voice he has.
taboos: will not let the chest be opened by anybody else, including a guild head
will not sign a custody entry that does not describe what physically happened
refuses to be examined by a party with standing to gain from the answer
will not discuss the currency, on the grounds that it is not his office's question

relationships.note: The account is held with continuous custody, which is its whole strength and the reason it is taught rather than proven, and its evidence is a continuous ore ledger reaching back before the first census. His ledger is that evidence, and one leaf of it is in his handwriting because the original could not be lifted.

That account has no custodian, which is why the challenge is always better sourced and always loses, and it is the only reading under which the later ascent was irreversible. He has kept a rival alive for four decades without ever reading it, and has declined to be sent it.

Every later tier is a receipt for the same payment, so the question is not one omission but the omission at the bottom of a column running to the present, and no surviving record names the payer. His ledger has four centuries of currency and no payer column, which is the omission itself.

That house sells capacity, keeping a roster of names whose labour is worth more than any individual contract, and it is the beneficiary of the rescue reading of its own founding because that reading gives it a merit rather than a debt. He keeps the ledger that makes the merit defensible, and he has never asked whether the merit is owed.

The grief is arithmetic if the seam was exhausted, and that account is the taught one and is uncontested by anybody with standing, which is precisely why it has never been tested against a claim. His ledger's span is the span the arithmetic runs on, so it is the document that makes four centuries of ascent look economic rather than forced.

The density that makes a stoneborn durable is the density that will not let a dantian form, so he carries the most load in the setting and cannot cultivate a mind practice at all. A mind cultivation of this record would have found the leaf four centuries ago, which is the one thing about his species that he has never resented and thinks about constantly.

That house answers access with a ledger and files everything, and it rivals the ironpact over the harbour tariffs because one of them writes the contract and the other decides what it is worth. The guild that writes every contract cannot afford a document with a page of substituted handwriting in it.

reference_stats.summary: A dense, slow, immensely durable frame carrying load rather than applying force, and he carries the heaviest object in the setting. Fights as an immovable mass that gets there eventually. Treat him as something you cannot hurry, cannot shake, and can only move by moving whatever he has decided to be standing on.
strengths: The densest durable frame on the plains, so nothing of ordinary strength shifts him and he can hold a position indefinitely
Enormously strong for his mass, which makes the heaviest object in the setting a burden rather than a lift
Does not tire, does not bend and does not need to breathe hard, so a long fight costs him nothing
Cannot be frightened out of a custody, because there is no interior for the fear to work through
weaknesses: Ceases short of the immortal tier because the density will not let a dantian form, so anything cultivated past him is a different class of threat
No dantian means no qi reserve and no technique, so every defence he has is structural
Very slow, which is the only thing an attacker needs and the only thing about him that is ever exploitable
Spends his entire life on one document and has no other competence whatsoever
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no technique to bring, because there is nothing inside him to address. Bring reach, because he closes distance at a pace you can walk backwards from, and bring weight, because a stoneborn's durability is a material property rather than a discipline. Never make him choose between the object and the fight, because he will always choose the object and you will not be the reason he stops.
notes: The lead chest is carried on his back and has been for thirty-one years, which has left a permanent structural dent in his own shoulder.
No stat line models a body whose single competence is custody, and the absence is deliberate.
